html:
The Tây Sơn rebellion was a peasant rising begun in 1771 by three brothers from Tây Sơn in central Vietnam, which overthrew both the Nguyễn lords of the south and the Trịnh lords and Lê emperors of the north.

The brothers promised to share out land and punish corrupt officials. They took Saigon, crushed a Siamese army in 1785, and marched on Hanoi. When the Qing sent an army to restore the Lê, the middle brother, Nguyễn Huệ, crowned himself Emperor Quang Trung and destroyed it at the battle of Ngọc Hồi-Đống Đa during the Tết new year of 1789.

Quang Trung began reforms, using Vietnamese script in official papers, but died in 1792. The surviving Nguyễn prince Nguyễn Ánh, with French help, fought back and took Hanoi in 1802. Vietnamese still celebrate Quang Trung as a national hero, alongside Trần Hưng Đạo.
sum: The Tây Sơn rebellion was a peasant rising begun in 1771 by three brothers from Tây Sơn in central Vietnam, which overthrew both the Nguyễn lords of the south and the Trịnh lords and Lê emperors of the north.
